text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM pressures the Dutch government for a decision on new location for a national airport to replace Schiphol airport. (p1).
- Rabobank chairman Wijffels says reform of European agricultural policy is too slow (p1).
- Dollar anticipates possible U.S. rate hike (p1).
- Senate is to vote on economic affairs minister Hans Wijers' competition law (p1).
- Court rules that energy companies are responsible for damage caused by power failures (p3).
- Dutch shipbuilding and repair industry has managed to keep its position in the world market (p3). DE VOLKSKRANT
- Group of Russian and Chinese investors study a restart of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker (2).
- KPN chief Wim Dik declines to head list of candidates for social democratic party D66 (p3).
- Killing piglets to stop swine fever is no solution for ending the epidemic, according to farmers' association (p3). DE TELEGRAAF
- Parliament threatens enquiry into last year's army aircraft disaster in which 34 people died (p1). ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Transport of dangerous substances often not according to regulations (p1).
- Traffic minister Annesmarie Jorritsma sticks to her agreement with parliament on Schiphol Airport's future (p11). TROUW
Chelsea wins Britain's FA Cup Final with Ruud Gullit as manager (p1)
Largest Dutch association of insurers' agents NVA calls for more clarity in life insurance performance.
